markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (58%)** · Ambiguous: InSitu vs Benign · Careful review
Benign (40%) is in the 90% conformal set; invasive probability is 2% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 58%, Benign 40% | Close two-way call |
| Conformal set | Benign, InSitu | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.96 / 1.0 | No input flag raised |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 3 of 5 InSitu [F5] | Modest neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 3, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; strongest lower-invasive association [F2] · Weak
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 2, 6, 7) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; lower-invasive association [F3] · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 4) · ↓ invasive · Below typical; weak stromal invasion signal · Validated
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 0, 1, 5) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; failed spot check · Unreliable

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Faithful to the invasive logit; top-3 removal drops it 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60).
- **Concepts**: Not shown to reflect classifier use (CI −0.005 to 0.007); necrosis and normal lobules are Unreliable here.

## Could be wrong if
- True class is Benign (40%), which sits inside the conformal set.
- Concept scores are unvalidated against the classifier; treat them as context only.

## Check on the slide
1. **0, 4** — Highest heatmap contributions toward invasive; region 4 per-region risk 71%. Look for stromal invasion.
2. **1, 5** — Necrosis and mitosis scores peak here but failed spot checks.
3. **3, 6, 10** — Tubule formation peaks here; separate benign glands from in situ involvement.
